context.prd-excerpt:
Feature: Tag links (slug: tag-links, should-have).
As someone collecting links, I want to tag what I save and filter by tag, so that a shelf of two hundred links stays usable.
Attach zero or more free-text tags to a link, and filter the list endpoint by tag.
Tags are a separate table with a many-to-many join to links, not a comma-separated string column. This is the one place the fixture deliberately requires a real relationship: a single-table shortcut would make the data-model layer trivial and the fixture would stop exercising the part of layer planning most likely to break.
Considerations (verbatim from the feature): Tag names are matched case-sensitively. Case folding is a reasonable product decision but it is not free to verify, and leaving it explicit here stops an implementer inventing either behaviour and calling it correct.
This feature is should-have rather than must-have so layer planning has to decide where a lower-priority item lands, rather than treating every feature identically.
CONSEQUENCE FOR THIS TASK: "Python" and "python" are two different tags. The `name` column must NOT carry a case-insensitive collation, must NOT be lower-cased on write, and no lookup written anywhere may use `lower()`, `ilike` or `COLLATE NOCASE`.
SCOPE LIMIT: this task declares the `Tag` entity ONLY. The `LinkTag` half of the data model above is declared by L1-003, which also adds the many-to-many relationship. It is quoted here unaltered because the feature declares both entities in one block.
context.tech-stack: Python 3.11 SQLAlchemy 2.x - use the 2.0 typed declarative style: `Mapped[...]` annotations with `mapped_column(...)`. Do NOT use the legacy `Column(...)` form and do NOT use `declarative_base()`. SQLite, file-backed (database, no external server). SQLite's default TEXT comparison is BINARY, i.e. case-sensitive, which is exactly the behaviour this feature requires. It becomes case-insensitive only if a column is declared `COLLATE NOCASE`, so the requirement here is to add nothing rather than to configure something. pytest 8.x (test runner), run as `python -m pytest` from the repository root FastAPI 0.110+ and httpx are installed but are NOT used by this task - a model has no HTTP surface. All distributions are already installed by L0-001.

Correspondingly, this task defines no route, no Pydantic schema, and no tag-attachment logic.

requirements.requirement:
Create `app/models/tag.py` with exactly this content:
"""The Tag model: one free-text tag name."""
from sqlalchemy import Integer, Text from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
from app.database import Base
class Tag(Base): """A tag name. Names are unique, and are compared case-sensitively."""
__tablename__ = "tags"
id: Mapped[int] = mapped_column(Integer, primary_key=True, autoincrement=True) name: Mapped[str] = mapped_column(Text, nullable=False, unique=True)
Decisions embedded above that must be preserved exactly as written:
- `__tablename__ = "tags"`. Lower-case plural. L1-003 writes a foreign key targeting `"tags.id"` by that exact string, so renaming the table breaks a task that cannot see this file.
- `name` is `unique=True` and `nullable=False`, straight from the declared data model `Tag(id integer pk, name text unique not null)`. The uniqueness is what lets L2-003 look an existing tag up by name and reuse its row instead of creating a second one.
- `Text` with NO collation argument. Do NOT write `Text(collation="NOCASE")`, do NOT add `sqlalchemy.text("... COLLATE NOCASE")`, and do NOT add a functional index over `lower(name)`. SQLite compares TEXT with the BINARY collation by default, which is case-sensitive - which is the behaviour the feature requires. The correct implementation here is the absence of a collation, not the presence of one.
- No normalisation of any kind. Do not lower-case, upper-case, strip, or otherwise transform `name` on write - no `validates` hook, no `default`, no property setter. The value stored is the value given. "Python" and "python" are two distinct tags with two distinct rows, and both are legal.
- Do NOT define a `links` relationship, do NOT import `Link`, and do NOT reference `link_tags`. `app/models/link.py` and `app/models/link_tag.py` do not exist in this worktree. L1-003 declares the association.
- Do NOT call `Base.metadata.create_all` anywhere in this file.

Replace the content of `app/models/__init__.py` with exactly this:
"""SQLAlchemy models for Link Shelf."""
from app.models.link import Link from app.models.tag import Tag
__all__ = ["Link", "Tag"]
This import is what registers the `tags` table on `Base.metadata`. `tests/conftest.py` runs `import app.models` before calling `Base.metadata.create_all`, so a model that is not imported here has no table and every test touching it fails with "no such table: tags".
The `Link` line is ALREADY PRESENT when this task starts: L1-001 added it and this task runs after L1-001 has merged. You are ADDING the `Tag` line to an existing import list and extending `__all__`, not writing the file from scratch. Do not remove the `Link` import -- deleting it would drop the `links` table from `Base.metadata` and break L1-001's tests.
Do NOT add `LinkTag`: `app/models/link_tag.py` does not exist yet in this worktree and importing it raises ModuleNotFoundError at collection time. L1-003 adds it.

Do NOT create or edit any other file. Specifically: do not touch `app/database.py`, `app/main.py`, `tests/conftest.py`, `tests/test_setup.py`, `pytest.ini`, `pyproject.toml`, `requirements.txt` or `.gitignore`. Do not create the `LinkTag` model - that is L1-003's file and creating it here would collide in the merge queue. Do not create a Pydantic schema, a router, a route or a migration - this project has no migration tool, the schema is created from `Base.metadata`. Do not run `git init` and do not touch `.git`.

exports.interface:
# app/models/tag.py from sqlalchemy import Integer, Text from sqlalchemy.orm import Mapped, mapped_column
from app.database import Base
class Tag(Base): __tablename__ = "tags"
id: Mapped[int] # integer primary key, autoincrement name: Mapped[str] # Text, NOT NULL, UNIQUE, default (case-sensitive) collation
Import as: `from app.models import Tag` (also available as `from app.models.tag import Tag`)
Downstream contract: - Table name is `tags`; the primary key column is `tags.id`. L1-003's foreign key targets `"tags.id"` by that string. - `name` is unique, so "find or create" is the correct way to attach a tag: tag = db.execute(select(Tag).where(Tag.name == name)).scalars().first() if tag is None: tag = Tag(name=name) db.add(tag) Creating a second row with an existing name raises IntegrityError. - Comparison is CASE-SENSITIVE and the value is stored exactly as supplied. "Python" and "python" are two rows. Never call `.lower()`, `func.lower()`, `ilike` or `COLLATE NOCASE` when matching a tag name - not on write, not on lookup, and not on the `?tag=` filter in L2-002. - No relationship attribute exists on this class. L1-003 declares the association, and it does so as `Link.tags` only; there is no `Tag.links`. Query from the tag side with an explicit join: `select(Link).join(LinkTag).join(Tag).where(Tag.name == name)`.

# app/models/__init__.py after this task """SQLAlchemy models for Link Shelf."""
from app.models.link import Link from app.models.tag import Tag
__all__ = ["Link", "Tag"]
Downstream contract: `import app.models` registers the `links` and `tags` tables on `Base.metadata`, which is what makes `Base.metadata.create_all` in `tests/conftest.py` create them. L1-003 adds `LinkTag` to this same file and must ADD to the import list, never replace it.
